series.name: Qualifying Hedge Funds: calculates alternative to VaR (count)
series.notes: The data are aggregated responses to SEC Form PF. Blank or null values are intentional to avoid potential disclosure of proprietary information of individual filers. Only responses from Qualifying Hedge Funds are included. Counts are based on SEC Form PF questions 40(a) and 41. Reporting funds disclose in question 40(a) if they regularly calculate VaR, or value at risk. VaR measures the maximum loss that a portfolio or investment is expected to suffer over a given time period at a specified confidence level. Many reporting funds use risk metrics other than, or in addition to, VaR. This information is disclosed in question 41. See additional definitions and methodology on the SEC Form PF Data Sets page of the Hedge Fund Monitor.

For example, hedge funds generally must post more collateral when they borrow from a prime brokerage than when they borrow in the repo market. series.name: Survey: lender balance sheet capacity as most important reason for a change in credit terms (net count of respondents)
series.notes: The data are derived from responses to question 6 of the Federal Reserve Board’s quarterly Senior Credit Officer Opinion Survey on Dealer Financing Terms (SCOOS). The net count represents the count of dealers citing each reason as the ‘most important’ cause for tightening the credit terms offered to hedge funds minus those citing the same reason as the most important reason for easing credit terms. A positive net count indicates the reason was a cause for an overall tightening of credit terms compared with the prior quarter, while a negative net count indicates it was a cause for easing over the same period. A zero net count signifies that no respondents cited the reason as the ‘most important’ or that an equal number cited it for both tightening and easing. See additional definitions and methodology on the SCOOS Data Sets page of the Hedge Fund Monitor.

series.name: Sponsored repo: repo volume (U.S. dollars)
series.notes: The data are aggregated daily repurchase agreement volumes transacted via the Fixed Income Clearing Corporation’s (FICC) sponsored repo platform. Sponsored repos are secured borrowing transactions where FICC-member dealers sponsor non-dealer counterparties (e.g., hedge funds) that need to borrow cash. Sponsored reverse repos are secured borrowing transactions where FICC-member dealers sponsor non-dealer counterparties (e.g., money market funds) that want to lend cash. Sponsored repo and reverse repo transactions are centrally cleared via FICC’s sponsored platform. Hedge funds borrowing cash comprise the majority of sponsored repo volumes, whereas money market funds lending cash comprise the majority of sponsored reverse repo volumes. See additional definitions and methodology on the Sponsored Repo Data Sets page of the Hedge Fund Monitor.
